Lina (PM): Heads-up: shipping private-deploy GA in Q3 requires a clear network-mode decision. Field asks split: some require static tenant IPs for firewall allowlists, others want zero-NetOps installs. Propose 3-mode surface: relay (default), preserve (opt-in peering), managed-nat (hybrid w/ SNAT per-tenant). Need launch criteria, upgrade story, and a short field checklist by EOM.
Diego (Eng): TL;DR on tradeoffs: relay = simplest install, control plane isolation, extra egress hops. preserve = best end-to-end latency but heavy NetOps and peering fragility. managed-nat = compromise: keep single egress IP per tenant but avoid full BGP.
Sam (Solutions): Field input: enterprise A wants preserve. Startup B prefers managed-nat. Mid-market prefers relay. We should publish a decision rubric so sales can qualify.
Noah (SRE): Operational concerns: preserve needs cross-account peering + BGP sessions we must monitor. managed-nat requires per-tenant SNAT pools and rotation; we'll need quotas. Relay adds measurable tail latency — we should quantify.
Diego (Eng): Proposal for rollout:
- GA: ship relay + managed-nat; preserve gated beta behind NetOps runbook and operator >=1.3.0.
- Post-GA: automated peering templates and peering sanity checks for preserve.
Lina (PM): Why gate preserve?
Diego (Eng): Two reasons: (1) upgrade & conflict risk (CIDR overlap), (2) support variance. We need preflight and a dry-run mode.
Sam (Solutions): I'll draft a short pre-sales rubric: recommended mode by customer profile + checklist items. Also sample firewall allowlist text for both managed-nat and preserve.
Noah (SRE): Metrics to add: "egress_hop_ms_p95", "peering_bgp_flaps_per_hour", "snat_pool_exhaustion". Add alarms and per-tenant dashboards.
Lina (PM): Upgrade compatibility: if a customer switches modes later, what is the safe path?
Diego (Eng): Safe switch flow (high level):
1) preflight CIDR/route checks (--preflight-check).
2) provision shadow resources (SNAT pool or peering stub).
3) traffic mirror for 10m to validate routing and TLS.
4) cutover during maintenance window, with automatic rollback on health failure.
We will require operator >=1.3.0 for preserve, >=1.2.0 for managed-nat, relay works back to 1.0.x.
Sam (Solutions): Can we include sample CLI snippets for docs?
Diego (Eng): Yep: relay install minimal:
```bash
./redwood-installer --network-mode relay --region eu-west-1 --operator-version=1.2.0
```
managed-nat preflight:
```bash
./redwood-installer --network-mode managed-nat --preflight --snat-pool=10.10.0.0/24
```
preserve dry-run:
```bash
./redwood-installer --network-mode preserve --preflight-only --reserved-cidrs=10.20.0.0/24
```
Noah (SRE): Also publish a short runbook for customer NetOps: e.g., required peering ASN, expected TCP ports, sample BGP policy. I'll draft.
Lina (PM): Action items: 1) Diego: spec preflight & shadow-provision flow + compatibility matrix (due in 6 working days). 2) Sam: pre-sales rubric + firewall text + customer mode recommend guide (due in 3 working days). 3) Noah: SLIs + per-tenant dashboard example + alert thresholds (due in 7 working days). 4) Lina: public docs stub + decision rubric to share with GTM (due in 5 working days).
Deploy-bot: Reminder set: "priv-deploy-network-modes-review" on 2024-07-18 15:00 UTC.
Sam (Solutions): One small UX ask: make the mode visible in console with a short explanative tooltip and an override option needing admin consent. I'll add a mock.
Diego (Eng): Note on costs: managed-nat reduces egress multiplier vs relay, preserve is cheapest for in-region pathing. We'll add a cost-estimator table to docs.
Lina (PM): OK locking this thread for the decision snapshot. We'll update after specs land. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
